notes: The session's web-search allowance ran out early in this part, so most pages were opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent: the Colorado Judicial Branch's judge pages, the Secretary of State's abstracts of votes, party pages and campaign sites. A few campaign addresses were tried by name; an address is listed only where the site itself was opened and names the candidate and the office.

Refused the reader, so nothing was taken from them and nothing was worked around: judicialperformance.colorado.gov (403: no judicial performance evaluations), colorado.gov/governor and governorsoffice.colorado.gov (403: the Governor's appointment releases), bioguide.congress.gov and congress.gov (403), carolynbarnes.com, danacharles4colorado.com and jeffcogop.org (429).

Joe Johnson (Libertarian, CU Regent CD6): a Joe Johnson ran as a Libertarian for State House District 63 in 2018 and 2020 and District 19 in 2022 (Secretary of State abstracts), but nothing ties that person to this race beyond the name and the party, so nothing was recorded. The Libertarian Party of Colorado links his name to a page on its own Canva account and Janet Turner's to a PDF on its own site; neither is a campaign website, and the party's page says 'Candidates 2026', not endorsed.

Judge LaQunya Latrese Baker-McKay: the Judicial Branch's page names her 'Laqunya Baker', District Court Judge in Arapahoe County (the 18th Judicial District is Arapahoe County alone since 2025); the given name, the court and the district tie her to this retention vote.
Eliza Hamrick's campaign site names her and 'Colorado House District 61' but carries a 2022 copyright line and no 2026 date: it is the campaign's standing site.

Nothing beyond what they filed for Kristopher Johnson, Justine Sandoval, Carolyn Barnes, Steve Harkess, Dana Charles, Janet Turner and Joe Johnson; no campaign site found for the sitting members Cecelia Espenoza (ceceliaespenoza.com shows only 'Coming Soon') and Rick Taggart.

Read and left out on purpose: jobs (deputy district attorney, assistant county attorney, public defender, law clerk, dispatcher, analyst), a party post (Doug Jones, Libertarian Party of Colorado vice chair, kept only inside his own words), Greg Lopez's 1992 Parker mayoral run 'as a Democrat' (a town election is nonpartisan, so it is not a party label on the record), and an NRA rating on Rebecca Winegar's site.
